root_cause.text: The original code used short-circuit evaluation with logical OR (||) in an if condition, so that `test_and_clear_bit` calls for later condition effects (FF_DAMPER, FF_FRICTION, FF_INERTIA) were skipped if an earlier bit was set and cleared, leaving those bits uncleared in the device's ffbit mask and leading to NULL pointer dereferences.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes from `if (test_and_clear_bit(FF_SPRING, dev->ffbit) || test_and_clear_bit(FF_DAMPER, dev->ffbit) || ...)` to using a boolean variable that accumulates results with `|=`, ensuring each `test_and_clear_bit` is unconditionally executed. The commit message explicitly states: "NULL pointer dereferences were happening because not all the conditional effects bits were cleared."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix short-circuit bug that prevented clearing all unsupported condition effect bits when an unknown layout is detected.
intent_record.what: Replaced a short-circuit OR of four test_and_clear_bit calls inside an if condition with a non-short-circuit accumulator variable that ORs the results and then checks the accumulator.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the new code always calls test_and_clear_bit for all four effect bits (FF_SPRING, FF_DAMPER, FF_FRICTION, FF_INERTIA) regardless of previous results, ensuring all set bits are cleared. The old code stopped after the first true result due to short-circuit evaluation, leaving later set bits uncleared.
